rationale.complete: Round 2 done (2026-10-05): dated pre-registration, synthetic validation on real call skeletons (fitted-field, call-length and planted worlds; 400 call-level runs, 24 Cox-field runs) with a dated amendment before real data, call-level two-layer design with a call-skeleton null on 71 units, Cox-field Hawkes refits with held-out folds on 71 units, thread-controlled named check, 621 estimates rows, period blocks. Reserved data not run; no natural experiment in round 2.
rationale.faithfulness: The named read-out kernel now beats a fitted Cox field held out (19/23 regime-III units, survival 0.90 vs 0.67 for planted coupling) and the call-skeleton null; half of it holds outside exchanges in progress (cold 0.046 vs thread 0.091). H03's exponential cross term is mostly field (survival 0.22). Timing effect fragile and mediated by the mark. Scorecard A1 B1 C2 D1 E0 F2 G1 H2 I0.
rationale.usefulness: Two operator handles with numbers: naming an agent adds 0.076 talk at its next call (0.046 outside an exchange), and a message cannot start a call, only change what the next call does. One analyst rule: judge cross-excitation against a fitted common field; shift nulls and shared within-day shapes leave H03-style triggering in place.

one_line: Reading changes what the next call does, not when it comes: a named read adds 0.076 talk at the read-out call (half outside any exchange), and this named kernel survives a fitted Cox field while H03's exponential cross term does not.

models.note: general kernel is field (survival 0.22); named kernel survives (0.90)

v2.claim: Once each agent's own call clock and call class are modelled, talk cross-excitation from read messages is near zero (median n_cross 0.004 vs 0.061 for H03's exponential kernel; below the synthetic shared-field floor 0.05 in all but one period), and the call-clock world beats the H03 world on held-out likelihood in 57/57 units.

ladder.factor: base: secondary (comparison pre-registered as P3; world B estimator added in A1 / A3 after smoke fits and the synthetic)
replication and rival beaten held out, one design counted once (call-clock world wins 57/57 units)
identified: world B recovers planted read-out excitation (15/16 within +/-25%), so effects >= 0.15 would be seen
partly robust (call-start bounds and edge trims change nothing; one estimator family)
penalty: shift / day-block nulls miss a shared 15-min field; floor from one synthetic strength

v2.decision: science model choice / detection: model each agent's call schedule and call class before fitting influence or branching models to agent logs
v2.magnitude: material (apparent cross-excitation falls from 0.061 to 0.004 per message once the call clock is modelled)
v2.generality: read-out-gated swarms (0); readiness not credited (needs the context ledger; call starts calibrated for most agents)
v2.rater: adjudicated 2026-10-04 (coordinator vs blind rater; see adjudication note)

raters.claim: Scope: 71 non-holdout units (35 periods). Once each agent's own call clock and call class are modelled, read-out-anchored cross-excitation between agents is near zero (n_cross ~0.004 vs 0.061 for H03's exponential kernel); the call-clock world wins by ~1.1 nats per held-out message in 57/57 units.

ladder.factor: replication and rival beaten held out: call-clock world wins 57/57 units (one design, credited once)
identified: synthetic recovers planted read-out excitation only in the call-clock world
null mis-sized: shift/day-block nulls do not control a shared 15-min field (G1 failed)
partly robust: call-start bound sensitivity changes nothing
penalty: world B excludes by construction influence through call timing/class

v2.scope: 71 non-holdout units (35 periods), TALK; conditional on call times and classes; the post hoc named-message effect is excluded
v2.adjudication_note: V judgement: the coordinator read the result as a small modelling note (V 2), the blind rater as a large, general rule for anyone inferring influence from timestamps (V 3.5); the rater also flagged it fragile because the pre-registered world gave the opposite sign. Ruling: the pre-registered world failed its own synthetic guard, so it is not a reasonable variant and fragile is false; replication and the held-out rival win are one design; V is material for analysts' model choice, without readiness credit because the call clock needs the ledger.
